patient.name: Eleanor Papadakis
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe shortness of breath, sudden onset

history.hpi: Daughter reports the patient woke up gasping for air about 20 minutes ago, much worse than her usual mild ankle swelling. She has been coughing up pink, frothy sputum. No chest pain reported.
history.events: Daughter woke to the patient gasping for air and called 911 immediately

scene.location: Single-story home, bedroom, patient sitting on the edge of the bed
scene.bystanders: Daughter present, extremely anxious, providing history
visualCues: Patient sitting bolt upright on edge of bed, gasping for air
Pink, frothy sputum at the mouth
Audible wet, crackling breath sounds without a stethoscope

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds an 81-year-old female in severe respiratory distress with pink frothy sputum, JVD, and profound hypertension, consistent with acute hypertensive pulmonary edema.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Severe distress, bilateral rales audible without auscultation, pink frothy sputum
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, bounding, tachycardic; JVD visible
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, extremely anxious and agitated
otherFindings: Sudden onset ~20 minutes ago, worse than usual baseline edema
Pink, frothy sputum at the mouth
Jugular venous distention visible while upright
Extreme air hunger, unable to speak in full sentences

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate CPAP for severe pulmonary edema, before or simultaneous with medication therapy
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Restoration of adequate oxygenation and ventilation should precede or be accomplished simultaneously with other medication therapies below. CPAP/BiPAP: See Airway Management Guideline for goals of care and escalation of interventions
expectedActions.rationale: Restoring oxygenation is the first priority in acute pulmonary edema, alongside afterload reduction.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Screen for phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use (sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil) within the past 48 hours before giving nitrates
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours. Examples are sildenafil, vardenafil and tadalafil, which are used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension
expectedActions.rationale: Combining nitrates with PDE5 inhibitors can cause profound, refractory hypotension.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL (SBP ≥160), may repeat every 5 minutes while SBP >100; consider IV nitro infusion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP >= 160 mmHg or MAP greater than 120: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg. Consider IV nitroglycerin infusion titrated to blood pressure
expectedActions.rationale: Rapid afterload and preload reduction with high-dose nitrates is the primary treatment for hypertensive pulmonary edema.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: Crew initiates CPAP simultaneously with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin (given the severely elevated blood pressure), after screening for phosphodiesterase inhibitor use.
Crew initiates CPAP but delays nitroglycerin, leaving the severely elevated afterload untreated and allowing the pulmonary edema to worsen.

phases.name: CPAP and high-dose nitro started
phases.description: Crew initiates CPAP for oxygenation while simultaneously screening for phosphodiesterase inhibitor use and administering high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin given the severely elevated blood pressure, considering an IV nitroglycerin infusion for continued titration.
phases.triggerCondition: The severity of hypertension (SBP ≥160/MAP >120) with acute pulmonary edema meets criteria for the high-dose nitroglycerin pathway alongside CPAP.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, blood pressure trending down
otherFindings: No PDE5 inhibitor use in the past 48 hours confirmed
First dose of sublingual nitroglycerin given

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal throughout transport until hospital CPAP is ready to take over
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Once initiated and patient is tolerating mask, DO NOT discontinue CPAP/BiPAP until patient is on the emergency department stretcher and hospital CPAP/BiPAP is immediately available for patient to be switched over, or physician is at bedside and requesting CPAP/BiPAP be discontinued
expectedActions.rationale: Interrupting CPAP can cause rapid decompensation from atelectasis and alveolar collapse.

transitions.if: CPAP seal maintained, BP improving, transport
transitions.condition: With CPAP and repeated high-dose nitroglycerin, blood pressure and oxygenation continue trending toward goal; crew prepares for transport.

phases.name: CPAP seal maintained, BP improving, transport
phases.description: With continued CPAP and titrated nitroglycerin, blood pressure and oxygenation trend toward goal. Crew maintains the CPAP mask seal continuously throughout transport per protocol.
phases.triggerCondition: Repeated nitroglycerin dosing and continuous CPAP have reduced afterload and improved oxygenation; the patient is prepared for transport.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Much improved, minimal accessory muscle use
otherFindings: CPAP seal maintained continuously since initiation
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Thank you, I can breathe so much better."

phases.name: Nitro delayed despite severe hypertension
phases.description: Crew initiates CPAP but delays nitroglycerin administration. Without afterload reduction, blood pressure remains severely elevated and pulmonary edema continues to worsen despite oxygen support.
phases.triggerCondition: CPAP alone does not address the underlying severely elevated afterload driving the pulmonary edema; without nitroglycerin, the patient's oxygenation and work of breathing continue to deteriorate.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Worsening despite CPAP, increasing frothy sputum
otherFindings: Blood pressure remains critically elevated without nitroglycerin
Increasing frothy sputum production despite CPAP

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize CPAP alone is insufficient; screen for PDE5 use and give high-dose nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP >= 160 mmHg or MAP greater than 120: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Severely elevated afterload requires pharmacologic reduction with nitrates; CPAP alone will not reverse hypertensive pulmonary edema.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)
